original_question: Do there exist universal infinitesimal symmetries Q(P) of Poisson structures that are nonlinear, proper, valid for all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds, and not produced from graph cocycles through Kontsevich’s orientation morphism O→r?
target_in_paper: The paper’s nearest matching target is the open problem, stated in the introductory summary of open problems, asking whether there exist graph-encoded universal infinitesimal deformations of Poisson brackets other than the known ones coming from Kontsevich’s orientation morphism applied to graph cocycles, such that these deformations are genuinely nontrivial on Poisson brackets (i.e. neither Poisson-cohomology trivial nor identically zero on Poisson inputs).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the topic as universal infinitesimal symmetries/deformations Q(P) of Poisson structures, correctly emphasizes nonlinearity and universality over all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds, and correctly points toward deformations not coming from known graph cocycles via Kontsevich’s orientation morphism. It also captures the paper’s concern with genuinely new, proper deformations rather than already known orientation-morphism examples.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation keeps the search within deformations that are still encoded by graphs; your draft could be read as allowing arbitrary nongraph constructions, which broadens the problem beyond the paper’s stated scope.
The paper explicitly excludes the trivial linear scaling P ↦ a·P before asking for other examples; this exclusion should be stated.
The paper formulates the problem in terms of infinitesimal deformations/deformations of Poisson brackets, written as Pdot = Q(P), not just abstract 'symmetries'.
The ambient category is finite-dimensional affine manifolds, implicitly real/affine in the Kontsevich setup; making this explicit improves faithfulness and self-containment.

The official nontriviality requirement is sharper than 'proper': the desired deformation should neither be Poisson-cohomology trivial nor vanish identically when the bracket being deformed is Poisson.
The paper phrases universality as 'universal w.r.t. all brackets' in the graph-encoded sense; this should be stated explicitly rather than only saying 'valid for all affine Poisson manifolds'.

Your draft says 'not produced from graph cocycles through Kontsevich’s orientation morphism'; the paper’s wording is slightly narrower: it asks for other graph-encoded universal deformations besides the known orientation-morphism ones, and characterizes the desired novelty by nontriviality/nonvanishing rather than only by non-origin from cocycles.
No definition of Poisson-cohomology triviality is given. If one wants the question fully stand-alone, one should signal that this means Q(P) represents a Poisson coboundary for Poisson P.
refined_question: Besides the trivial linear scaling P ↦ a·P and the at least countably many nonlinear graph-encoded universal infinitesimal deformations Pdot = Q(P) obtained from Grothendieck–Teichmüller-related cocycles in the unoriented graph complex via Kontsevich’s orientation morphism, do there exist any other graph-encoded universal infinitesimal deformations of Poisson brackets P on arbitrary finite-dimensional affine real manifolds such that, for Poisson P, the velocity Q(P) neither vanishes identically nor is Poisson-cohomology trivial?
justification: The draft is close, but the paper’s official target is narrower and more precise. It does not ask for arbitrary universal nonlinear symmetries outside the orientation-morphism image; it asks specifically for other deformations that are still graph-encoded and hence universal, after excluding the trivial scaling symmetry. The paper also makes the novelty criterion exact: such a deformation should be neither Poisson-cohomology trivial nor identically zero on Poisson brackets. This wording appears in the paper’s own summary of its open problems and is the nearest official formulation to your draft. The nearby context also stresses that the known nonlinear universal flows come from Grothendieck–Teichmüller-related graph cocycles via Kontsevich’s orientation morphism, which is why the refined question keeps that comparison explicit rather than broadening to all conceivable universal formulas.
